transcript:
Header: 2027-02-16 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Julia (RiverMark Eng Mgr), Leo (Platform Eng), Marcus (SRE)

Summary: Quick sync on latency numbers from last week's bench, tuning actions on TTFT and streaming, sequence length analysis, kernel selection options and next steps for dedicated pilot.

00:00 Samira: hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick check in — want to run through the benchmarks Ethan posted and then nail down the perf runs you want us to do next.
00:12 Julia: yep, thanks. busy week but saw the sheet, some of the numbers surprised us, TTFT still higher than we expected on the 6k token model.
00:25 Ethan: yeah so quick context, we ran three variants: hosted large (fp16), quantized int8, and a kernel-optimized build on the same infra. the TTFT is mainly impacted by model load + kv warmup for cold sessions. we also saw streaming improvements when we enable chunked streaming vs full-buffering.
00:48 Leo: when you say chunked streaming, is that the same as the incremental flush we tested where tokens get sent as partials? we noticed some garbled tokens in one run.
01:03 Ethan: correct, chunked streaming flushes at 64 token increments in our test; there was some truncation artifact because the tokenization boundary got misaligned — that's a config issue, not model. we can tune flush size and buffer thresholds.
01:20 Marcus: just to flag SLOs, our product team wants TTFT < 300ms p50 and p95 < 700ms for 64-token prompts, anything above that is risky for the UX.
01:35 Samira: understood — target is reasonable. Ethan, can you recap which knobs we touched last week?
01:42 Ethan: sure — prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts, reduced KV cache cold misses by ~30%. we adjusted batch windows to 10ms, disabled large sequence batching for low-latency flows, and tried kernel A vs kernel B — kernel A is the default cu-attn kernel, kernel B is experimental fused attention for short seqs. kernel B improved p50 by ~80ms on seq length 64 but regressed p95 on longer sequences ~512.
02:10 Julia: so kernel B helps short chats but hurts longer inference. our traffic is mixed, around 60% short (<128) and 30% medium (128-512) and 10% long (>512).
02:26 Ethan: exactly — that's why smart routing could help: route short sessions to instances with kernel B optimized binaries, long sessions to compiled builds tuned for long seqs.
02:40 Leo: is that routing something you can do with our Dedicated pool? we need to know if we can pin binaries per node.
02:50 Ethan: yes, Dedicated supports per-node model variants and kernel selection; you can pin a node-class with fused-attn kernels. there's a small capacity tax but it's doable.
03:05 Marcus: what about TTFT when we have cold caches for a new user? we saw 1.2s on average for cold.
03:15 Ethan: cold startup is dominated by library init + model shard load + KV allocation. we recommend a warmup strategy: periodic keep-alive on hot partitions and pre-warming popular model shards during expected traffic spikes. also keep small preforked inference workers for low-TTF.
03:40 Julia: for pre-warm, what's the memory cost? our infra is constrained, we can't hold many warm workers.
03:47 Ethan: fair — that's where smarter batching and streaming help: if you accept slightly lower throughput you can reduce resident warm workers. we can also provide a hybrid: minimal warm pool for p50-sensitive endpoints and burst autoscale for higher throughput.
04:05 Samira: let's talk concrete next bench. Julia, you said you'll send seq distribution, Ethan will run bench aligned to that distribution, and we will test two modes: streaming (chunked 64) and non-streaming (full buffer), seqs [64, 256, 512].
04:20 Julia: yes I'll upload the distribution to the sheet by tomorrow.
04:25 Ethan: i'll include TTFT, token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, and memory/ GPU utilization and kernel binary version.
04:35 Leo: also include the streaming jitter numbers — we want to see how often partial messages arrive delayed.
04:45 Ethan: will do. one more note: quantization (int8) cut median token cost by ~2x but added ~30-40ms overhead on first token for dequant ops; not huge but relevant to TTFT targets.
05:03 Marcus: so tradeoff: int8 saves cost but could push us over TTFT for tight UX endpoints.
05:12 Samira: that's part of the decision we'll help you make. for mission-critical chat flows maybe leave fp16, use int8 for background summarization jobs.
05:25 Julia: makes sense. can Redwood support per-route quantization decisions?
05:32 Ethan: yes, you can define route-level configs in the deployment manifest, including quantization profile, batch policy, and kernel hints.
05:44 Julia: on security, Marcus, any outstanding asks? we need SSO, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs preserved for 1 year.
05:56 Marcus: yes SSO via SAML, KMS for customer-managed keys, and audit export to our SIEM. also need SOC2 docs.
06:06 Samira: we'll share the security pack with SOC2, diagrams, and KMS integration notes. Dedicated supports BYOK and HSM through our KMS connectors.
06:20 Marcus: good. also curious if Redwood can provide more granular telemetry — we want token-level cost breakdowns for specific routes.
06:30 Ethan: that's already in Console — token-level cost + per-model latency distribution; we'll include a sample dashboard link.
06:40 Julia: perfect. one more performance question: you mentioned kernel selection automatic switch. can it be automated based on seq length?
06:50 Ethan: yes we have a smart routing policy that can inspect sequence length and route to the appropriate binary or fallback; it's policy-driven and can be part of Dedicated routing.
07:05 Leo: how fast is the switch? do we see added routing latency?
07:10 Ethan: sub-5ms routing decision; it's simply a lookup in the routing table and header rewrite. the heavy cost is model variant mismatch if the target node hasn't warmed the KV cache.
07:22 Julia: can you do a demo of smart routing and kernel selection?
07:28 Samira: we can schedule a technical deep dive — propose Thurs 2027-02-25 15:00 UTC, invite infra and SRE.
07:36 Julia: that works.
07:38 Samira: ok recap of deliverables — Ethan runs 1k bench across seq sizes and modes, Julia shares seq distribution, Samira sends pricing and security pack; schedule deep dive 2/25.
07:52 Marcus: ok thanks all, excited to see the numbers.
07:56 Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the sheet and slack.
